title: Throttling with SemaphoreSlim and Parallel.ForEachAsync
summary: Limit how much runs at once, always give the slot back, and pick between a semaphore and Parallel.ForEachAsync.

steps.title: A semaphore is a counter of free slots
body: `new SemaphoreSlim(2)` starts with **two slots**. `Wait()` (or `await WaitAsync(ct)`) takes a slot, or waits until one is free;
`Release()` gives one back. Unlike a lock, any number up to the count may be inside at once, and it is **not owned** by a thread
In the card, three threads share two slots. Step until T3 tries to enter: its lane turns into the red *blocked* hatch until
someone releases. **Try every interleaving**: `peak` (the most threads inside at once) is never 3.

options: If the call throws (or is cancelled) without it, the slot is never given back; after a few failures every caller waits forever
So that the exception is swallowed
steps.explain: A leaked slot is a slow-motion deadlock: the service works until enough calls have failed, then hangs. Note `WaitAsync` is *outside* the `try`: if waiting is cancelled you never got a slot, so you must not release one.

steps.title: Parallel.ForEachAsync for a known list
body: For "process this list, at most N at a time", .NET 6+ has it built in:
- `MaxDegreeOfParallelism` defaults to `Environment.ProcessorCount` for `ForEachAsync`: set it to what the *dependency* can take.
- The first exception **cancels the token** given to the other bodies and is rethrown when the loop ends.
- Results: collect into a `ConcurrentBag`, or into an array slot per index (each body writes its own slot, no race).
Use a **shared `SemaphoreSlim`** instead when the limit is about a resource shared by **many requests** ("at most 10 calls to the
vendor from this whole process"), not about one loop.

steps.explain: `Wait(0)` tries without waiting: it takes the last slot (True), then finds none (False). One `Release` frees one slot.

steps.title: Fetch everything, at most N at a time
prompt: Write **`static async Task<List<string>> FetchAllAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> urls, Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<string>> fetch, int maxConcurrent, CancellationToken ct)`**:
- call `fetch` for every url, with **at most `maxConcurrent`** calls in flight, and do use all of them;
- return the results **in the same order as `urls`**;
Use a `SemaphoreSlim` or `Parallel.ForEachAsync`. The tests hold every fetch until they have counted how many are in flight.

template: async Task<string> DojoFetch(string url, CancellationToken ct)
lock (dojoLock) { dojoCalls++; dojoInFlight++; dojoPeak = Math.Max(dojoPeak, dojoInFlight); }
for (var i = 0; i < 200 && Volatile.Read(ref dojoInFlight) < 3; i++) await Task.Delay(10);
Dojo.Eq("Three fetches are in flight while they wait", 3, Volatile.Read(ref dojoInFlight));
Dojo.Eq("Never more than 3 at once", 3, dojoPeak);
Dojo.Eq("Results come back in the order of the urls", dojoUrls.Select(u => "page " + u).ToList(), dojoResults);
hints: A `SemaphoreSlim(maxConcurrent)`: each url's task awaits `WaitAsync(ct)`, fetches inside `try`, releases in `finally`. `Task.WhenAll` keeps the order.
`var tasks = urls.Select(async url => { await gate.WaitAsync(ct); try { return await fetch(url, ct); } finally { gate.Release(); } });`
explain: `Task.WhenAll` returns results in the order of the tasks you gave it, not the order they finished, which is why the results line up
with `urls`. With `Parallel.ForEachAsync`, write each result into `results[index]` instead.
